story_review.one_viewing_summary: This is the planned chain, not observed pixels. Brown water tops a San Antonio curb and climbs a fence post to its orange ankle mark while the porch phone stays dark, then the warning lands late. The prototype station at the curb charges from the sun, and its dashed line toward a cell tower stops halfway. Water rises past its four lenses and each lights. The opened housing feeds the chip, which lights a large amber lamp and risk bar while a dark server across the road is never reached. Rings run down a long street to the hub and across open country to its mast, and a seated responder works at a flood map whose paths spread along the creek. On a curb notice board the whole 98.82% card fills and the assessments tag pins, then a blank field result card slides in. In the wider two-card view both cards stay readable while a hand stamps none reported on the blank one. A finger reads a blank paper map, and a technician latches the deployment plan into the prototype's case.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening asks whether a station can judge rising street water with no power line and no cell tower. The chain of charge, four lenses, on-chip judgment, radio to the hub and flood map answers yes as a disclosed design. The limits stay on the curb board and are now readable throughout: the reported validation figure stays whole beside a field result card stamped none reported, and the announcement names no installation. The close keeps the plan with the uninstalled prototype toward the stated goal, so no deployment outcome is invented.
story_review.weakest_transition: s7 to s8 at 49.2 s. The cut goes from the large single validation card to a still, wider two-card board where the action is carried only by the stamp entering, pressing and leaving. It should read as the same board pulled wider, but the near-hold framing and the 0.7 s still end before the map cut need the timed phone review to show they do not stall.
